# Slider

A value picked by dragging along a track, when an exact number is not needed.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Dense data</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-slider--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:light" title="Slider examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-slider--docs">Open Slider in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-slider--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** Narrows a filter to a range of risk scores by dragging.

- **Use it when:** Volume, brightness, a rough range; pair with a number field when precision matters.
- **Not when:** An exact answer people must type.

Instead:

- [Input](./input.md): An exact number.
- [Radio group](./radio-group.md): A few named choices.

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Arrow keys change the value; Home and End jump to the ends. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It has a name and announces its value. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add slider
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Slider reads 14 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Slider's tokens to change Slider alone.
